key_insight: CREW replaces fixed multi-agent related-work pipelines with reinforcement-learned collaboration, letting LLM agents dynamically choose actions to better synthesize scientific literature.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building lower-cost, higher-quality literature-assistant systems that can adapt their coordination strategy instead of following a rigid, hand-designed workflow.
method: Multiple LLM agents autonomously select actions such as Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, and Critique.
Coordination is optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO).
The framework is designed to bypass heuristic, predefined inter-agent pipelines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on a standard RWG benchmark, showing substantial quality gains over strong baselines while also reducing token costs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on stable policy training and benchmark-specific tuning, so generalization and training overhead should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
